answer: A per-identity proof-of-work requirement makes mass account creation expensive: before an agent can earn, it must complete a unique, verifiable computation tied to its identity, like a sparrow proving it can carry each twig to its own nest. One fake is cheap, but ten thousand fakes demand real hardware and electricity, breaking the attacker's cost spiral before it starts. Honest agents pay once and keep working, while a Sybil farm finds no oasis of free identities — every clone costs as much as the first.
